meta.title: GitHub access guide
meta.description: Sidebar panel that repairs access when only some server addresses are reachable. Start proxy runs a racing proxy on 127.0.0.1:17897 that dials every candidate address of a host at once and keeps the first that connects, then points the browser at it through a PAC: sites inside the scope use the proxy, everything else stays direct, and a listener that is down or unreachable falls back to DIRECT instead of breaking other sites. The scope card adds extra sites or turns on full mode so non-GitHub sites get the same racing. The system proxy, git's http.proxy and HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY all point at it; the previous values are snapshotted first and restored on stop or uninstall, with no administrator rights and no hosts edit. Repair instead installs a reversible git url.<channel>.insteadOf rewrite and only reports success after a plain-URL check passes. The panel also shows live channel status, converts GitHub URLs into forms this network can open, and documents symptoms, a five-minute self-check, hosts notes, SSH over 443 and common commands. Limits: works when individual addresses are blocked or unstable; a network that drops the whole range cannot be repaired this way; accelerator prefixes serve files and release archives, not the site itself.
